etymologies.etymologyHTML: From compose +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: One who, or that which, quiets or calms.

quote.citation: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter VI, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume III, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 43:
quote.text: The exertion necessary to soothe and subdue Lucy's passionate sorrow was the best composer to Francesca's own agitation.

quote.citation: 1713, Joseph Trapp, Musicus Apparatus Academicus set to music by William Croft, pages 38–41, →MDZ:
quote.text: Where, mighty Anna, will thy Glories end.Thou Great Composer of distracted states.
